main_conditions: Stage IV non-small cell lung cancer
Lung cancer with mediastinal nodal involvement
Stage IV adenocarcinoma of the lung
other_conditions: Hormone receptor-positive breast cancer in mother
expanded_sentences: The patient is a 53-year-old female diagnosed with metastatic non-small cell lung cancer, specifically adenocarcinoma, with liver metastases and mediastinal nodal involvement.
The patient presents with severe chronic cough and exertional dyspnea, symptoms that have been progressively worsening.
Elevated hepatic transaminase levels were noted, with mild increases in AST and ALT during systemic therapy monitoring.
The patient has a history of smoking, having smoked approximately 15 pack-years, and quit 7 years prior to diagnosis.
Tumor sequencing revealed an actionable EGFR exon 19 deletion, which is relevant for targeted therapy.
Osimertinib, an oral EGFR inhibitor, is being administered at a dose of 80 milligrams.
A CT-guided biopsy from the right upper lobe confirmed the diagnosis of lung adenocarcinoma.
Baseline CEA levels were measured at 42.7 nanograms per milliliter prior to initiating first-line systemic therapy.
The patient's mother was diagnosed with hormone receptor-positive breast cancer in her early sixties.
